notes: Overturn confirmed. Opposite a group the numeric operand is 'treated as though it were moved to a group item of the same size as the numeric data item (in terms of standard data format characters)' (GR2), and a numeric literal's size in those characters is its digit count (IV.4.2.2.2.2 GR4). So -5 opposite G2 (X(2)) is a one-character image padded with a space: whatever represents its sign within that character, it can never equal '-5'. The compiler compares the literal's source text: below 2002 ConditionRenderer.DropsOperationalSign is false when either operand is a group, and OperandText.AsItemSizeTemporary then returns AsString(deSign: false), which for a literal is "-5". The reader's 'storage characters, sign kept' reading is right for a data item (its overpunch lives in its digit characters) but a literal has no storage; its image is its digits. Rerun rel4: A NE, B EQ, C EQ, D NE, E NE, F [5 ]; B and C must be NE under any sign representation, and with the compiler's own one-character literal image ('5', as its MOVE -5 TO G2 stores in rel4) A, D and E must be EQ. Own probe i1.cob (two digits, three-character group): IF G3 = -12 is EQ for '-12' and NE for '12 ' (expected NE and EQ), the same in the statement form and nested in ELSE (R NE, S EQ). Note PB5419 is right in its citation, expected A-E and harm flags (wrong_answer, silent, MAJOR). Two corrections: (1) its 'nested in an ELSE compiled to Compare(G2.AsImage(), "5")' is not reproduced at this compiler: rel3 (whose line 13 is cut at column 72, COBOL6688, so the rest of the paragraph is nested in that ELSE) now prints G2M EQ, i.e. the comparison against '-5'; (2) the context dependence is real but in the MOVE: MOVE -5 TO G2 displays [-5] in rel3 and in own x1.cob, and [5 ] in rel4 and own x3.cob, where x1 and x3 differ only by rel3's lines 18-21 (MOVE "-5" TO E2 and IF E2 = -5); a group move of a one-digit literal cannot produce two characters, so MOVE of a signed numeric literal to a group is a sibling wrong answer the note should name (VI.6.19.4) and the 'compiler's own MOVE stores 5 ' premise holds only in some programs. kb/Work PB5419 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set7/decisions.json).

next.reason: 1985: "the numeric operand is treated as though it were moved to a group item of the same size as the numeric data item"; 2023: "For comparison, an alphanumeric group item shall be treated as an elementary alphanumeric data item.". 1985 compares the numeric as if group-moved, with no conversion and any sign kept. 2023 treats the group as elementary alphanumeric, so the elementary rule applies; the group-move case is gone.
